question.text: What should you do right after hitting an animal or finding an injured one?

answer.text: After hitting an animal or finding an injured one, pull safely to the roadside, stay in the car with the doors locked and turn on the hazard lights.

teaching.text: After an animal strike, pull safely to the roadside, stay inside with doors locked, and turn on the hazard lights. Remember: pull over, stay inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After hitting an animal or finding an injured one, pull safely to the roadside, stay in the car with the doors locked and turn on the hazard lights.

question.text: Should you walk up to an animal you have struck?

answer.text: Do not walk up to an animal you have struck, because it may be dangerous.

teaching.text: Do not walk up to an animal you struck, because it may be dangerous. Remember: keep away from it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not walk up to an animal you have struck, because it may be dangerous.

question.text: What is the first rule in any driving emergency?

answer.text: In any emergency, the first rule is not to panic but to react quickly and correctly.

teaching.text: In any emergency, do not panic; react quickly and correctly. Remember: do not panic.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In any emergency, the first rule is not to panic but to react quickly and correctly.

question.text: What should you do if the brakes fail in a manual car?

answer.text: If the brakes fail in a manual car, shift to a lower gear, release the clutch and apply the emergency brake.

teaching.text: In a manual car with failed brakes, shift down, release the clutch and apply the emergency brake. Remember: downshift, clutch out, emergency brake.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the brakes fail in a manual car, shift to a lower gear, release the clutch and apply the emergency brake.

question.text: What should you do if the brakes fail in an automatic car?

answer.text: If the brakes fail in an automatic car, apply the emergency brake and move the gear lever into the low range.

teaching.text: In an automatic with failed brakes, apply the emergency brake and move the lever into low range. Remember: emergency brake, low range.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the brakes fail in an automatic car, apply the emergency brake and move the gear lever into the low range.

question.text: How does the brake-failure response differ between manual and automatic cars?

answer.text: With failed brakes, a manual car downshifts and releases the clutch before the emergency brake, while an automatic applies the emergency brake and selects low range.

teaching.text: A manual downshifts and releases the clutch before the emergency brake, while an automatic uses the emergency brake and low range. Remember: manual downshifts first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With failed brakes, a manual car downshifts and releases the clutch before the emergency brake, while an automatic applies the emergency brake and selects low range.

question.text: Why use the emergency brake and low gear even if they may be damaged?

answer.text: Using the emergency brake and low gear this way may damage them, but with failed brakes there is no better option.

teaching.text: The emergency brake and low gear may be damaged, but with failed brakes there is no better option. Remember: no better option.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Using the emergency brake and low gear this way may damage them, but with failed brakes there is no better option.

question.text: How do you dry wet brakes?

answer.text: To dry wet brakes, drive a short distance while pressing lightly on the brake pedal so the friction heat evaporates the water.

teaching.text: Dry wet brakes by driving a short way while pressing lightly on the pedal. Remember: light pressure dries brakes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To dry wet brakes, drive a short distance while pressing lightly on the brake pedal so the friction heat evaporates the water.

question.text: How should you control speed on a long or steep downhill?

answer.text: On a long or steep downhill, control speed with a lower gear rather than the brake pedal, shifting down at the top before you start down.

teaching.text: On long or steep downhills, shift down at the top and let a lower gear hold your speed. Remember: gear down at the top.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a long or steep downhill, control speed with a lower gear rather than the brake pedal, shifting down at the top before you start down.

question.text: When do you use light brake pressure, and when do you spare the brakes with a low gear?

answer.text: Wet brakes are dried with light brake pressure over a short drive, while a long downhill calls for a lower gear instead of the brake pedal.

teaching.text: Light pedal pressure dries wet brakes, while a lower gear spares the pedal on long downhills. Remember: dry with brakes, descend in gear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wet brakes are dried with light brake pressure over a short drive, while a long downhill calls for a lower gear instead of the brake pedal.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: dry with brakes, descend in gear

question.text: What should you do if the gas pedal sticks?

answer.text: If the gas pedal sticks, tap it or lift it with your foot, shift to neutral and brake firmly without locking the wheels, then get completely off the road.

teaching.text: If the gas pedal sticks, tap or lift it, shift to neutral, brake firmly without locking the wheels, and get off the road. Remember: neutral, then brake firmly.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the gas pedal sticks, tap it or lift it with your foot, shift to neutral and brake firmly without locking the wheels, then get completely off the road.

question.text: How does handling a stuck gas pedal differ from handling failed brakes?

answer.text: A stuck gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral and braking firmly, whereas brake failure calls for a lower gear and the emergency brake.

teaching.text: A stuck pedal calls for neutral and firm braking, while failed brakes call for a low gear and the emergency brake. Remember: stuck throttle means neutral.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A stuck gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral and braking firmly, whereas brake failure calls for a lower gear and the emergency brake.

question.text: What are the signs of a tire problem and of a blowout?

answer.text: An unexplained bumpy ride is a reason to stop and check the tires; a blowout announces itself with a loud noise and a swerve.

teaching.text: An unexplained bumpy ride means stop and check the tires, and a blowout brings a loud noise and a swerve. Remember: bumpy ride, check tires.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An unexplained bumpy ride is a reason to stop and check the tires; a blowout announces itself with a loud noise and a swerve.

question.text: What should you do the moment a tire blows out?

answer.text: In a blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the car straight in your lane, then slow down by lifting off the accelerator.

teaching.text: In a blowout, grip the wheel, keep the car straight in your lane, and lift off the accelerator. Remember: grip, straight, lift off.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the car straight in your lane, then slow down by lifting off the accelerator.

question.text: When should you brake after a blowout?

answer.text: After a blowout, do not brake until the engine has slowed the car enough for you to keep control, then pull completely off the road.

teaching.text: Wait to brake until the engine has slowed the car enough for control, then pull completely off the road. Remember: brake after the engine slows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a blowout, do not brake until the engine has slowed the car enough for you to keep control, then pull completely off the road.

question.text: What should you do before changing a flat tire?

answer.text: Before changing a flat, move fully off the road, set the parking brake and put out flares if you have them.

teaching.text: Before changing a flat, get fully off the road, set the parking brake, and put out flares if you have them. Remember: fully off, brake set.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before changing a flat, move fully off the road, set the parking brake and put out flares if you have them.

question.text: How does the blowout response differ from the steps for changing a flat?

answer.text: During a blowout you hold the wheel straight and avoid braking until the engine slows the car, while a flat tire change starts only once the car is fully off the road.

teaching.text: During a blowout you hold straight and brake late, and a tire change waits until the car is fully off the road. Remember: driving response versus stopped change.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During a blowout you hold the wheel straight and avoid braking until the engine slows the car, while a flat tire change starts only once the car is fully off the road.

question.text: Where should passengers wait during a tire change?

answer.text: During a tire change, all passengers must get out on the passenger side and wait off the road, never standing in front of or behind the car.

teaching.text: Passengers get out on the passenger side and wait off the road, never in front of or behind the car. Remember: out the passenger side.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: During a tire change, all passengers must get out on the passenger side and wait off the road, never standing in front of or behind the car.

question.text: Which lights and safety steps keep the car from rolling during a tire change?

answer.text: Turn on the flashers and parking lights and block the wheels so the car cannot roll while the tire is changed.

teaching.text: Use the flashers and parking lights, and block the wheels so the car cannot roll. Remember: flashers on, block wheels.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Turn on the flashers and parking lights and block the wheels so the car cannot roll while the tire is changed.

question.text: Should you repair your car beside passing traffic?

answer.text: Never try to repair a car where it is exposed to passing traffic; call a tow truck or mechanic instead.

teaching.text: Never repair a car where it is exposed to traffic; call a tow truck or mechanic. Remember: call a tow instead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Never try to repair a car where it is exposed to passing traffic; call a tow truck or mechanic instead.

question.text: What should you and your passengers do after a breakdown?

answer.text: In a breakdown, move the car fully onto the shoulder, get everyone out on the passenger side and stand well away from the car, not in front of it or behind it.

teaching.text: In a breakdown, get fully onto the shoulder, everyone out the passenger side, and stand well away. Remember: shoulder, out, stand away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a breakdown, move the car fully onto the shoulder, get everyone out on the passenger side and stand well away from the car, not in front of it or behind it.

question.text: How do you signal that you need help after a breakdown?

answer.text: To ask for help after a breakdown, tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood; after dark use the parking lights or flashers.

teaching.text: Tie a white cloth to the left door handle or aerial and raise the hood, using lights after dark. Remember: white cloth, hood up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To ask for help after a breakdown, tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood; after dark use the parking lights or flashers.

question.text: What makes up the breakdown help signal, and which side do you exit?

answer.text: A breakdown signal for help is a white cloth on the left door handle or aerial plus a raised hood, and everyone exits on the passenger side.

teaching.text: The help signal is a white cloth plus a raised hood, with everyone out on the passenger side. Remember: cloth, hood, passenger side.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A breakdown signal for help is a white cloth on the left door handle or aerial plus a raised hood, and everyone exits on the passenger side.

question.text: What emergency items should always be in the car?

answer.text: Keep a flashlight or flares in the car at all times for emergencies.

teaching.text: Keep a flashlight or flares in the car at all times. Remember: flashlight or flares.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Keep a flashlight or flares in the car at all times for emergencies.

question.text: What should you do first if an oncoming car crosses into your path?

answer.text: If an oncoming vehicle crosses the center line into your path, slow down at once and sound the horn.

teaching.text: If an oncoming car crosses the center line into your path, slow down at once and sound the horn. Remember: slow down, sound horn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If an oncoming vehicle crosses the center line into your path, slow down at once and sound the horn.

question.text: Which way should you go when a vehicle crosses into your lane?

answer.text: When a vehicle crosses into your lane, keep to the right, even if that means leaving the road.

teaching.text: When a vehicle crosses into your lane, keep to the right, even if it means leaving the road. Remember: keep right, even off road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a vehicle crosses into your lane, keep to the right, even if that means leaving the road.

question.text: What should you avoid when your wheels drop onto the shoulder?

answer.text: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or jerk back toward the road, since you could skid or roll over.

teaching.text: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or jerk back, since you could skid or roll. Remember: no hard brakes, no jerks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or jerk back toward the road, since you could skid or roll over.

question.text: How do you safely return to the road after running onto the shoulder?

answer.text: To recover from running onto the shoulder, ease off the gas, steer straight, let the engine slow the car, and return gradually only once traffic is clear and you are nearly stopped.

teaching.text: Ease off the gas, steer straight, let the engine slow the car, and return gradually once nearly stopped. Remember: slow first, return gradually.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To recover from running onto the shoulder, ease off the gas, steer straight, let the engine slow the car, and return gradually only once traffic is clear and you are nearly stopped.

question.text: How does recovering from the shoulder differ from avoiding an oncoming car?

answer.text: Running onto the shoulder means no hard braking and no sharp turn back, while an oncoming car in your lane means keep right even off the road.

teaching.text: A shoulder drop calls for a gentle, gradual return, while an oncoming car calls for keeping right. Remember: shoulder gentle, oncoming keep right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Running onto the shoulder means no hard braking and no sharp turn back, while an oncoming car in your lane means keep right even off the road.

question.text: Which road surfaces make skids more likely?

answer.text: Wet roads, ice and packed snow make skids more likely, so reduce speed gradually on them.

teaching.text: Wet roads, ice and packed snow make skids more likely, so slow down gradually. Remember: wet, ice, packed snow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Wet roads, ice and packed snow make skids more likely, so reduce speed gradually on them.

question.text: How should you brake to avoid a skid with and without ABS?

answer.text: To avoid a skid with ABS, press the brake firmly and steadily without pumping; without ABS, pump the brakes gently.

teaching.text: With ABS, brake firmly and steadily; without ABS, pump the brakes gently. Remember: ABS steady, otherwise pump.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To avoid a skid with ABS, press the brake firmly and steadily without pumping; without ABS, pump the brakes gently.

question.text: How does braking to avoid a skid differ with and without ABS?

answer.text: With ABS you hold firm steady pressure to avoid a skid, but without ABS you pump the brakes gently.

teaching.text: Hold steady with ABS, and pump gently without it. Remember: hold with ABS, pump without.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With ABS you hold firm steady pressure to avoid a skid, but without ABS you pump the brakes gently.

question.text: Which way should you steer in a skid?

answer.text: In a skid, ease off the gas and steer toward the direction the rear of the car is sliding.

teaching.text: In a skid, ease off the gas and steer toward the direction the rear is sliding. Remember: steer where the rear slides.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a skid, ease off the gas and steer toward the direction the rear of the car is sliding.

question.text: What should you do as the car straightens out of a skid?

answer.text: As the car begins to straighten out of a skid, turn the wheel back the other way so you do not over-steer.

teaching.text: As the car straightens, turn the wheel back so you do not over-steer. Remember: steer back, avoid over-steer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: As the car begins to straighten out of a skid, turn the wheel back the other way so you do not over-steer.

question.text: What are the two steering moves in a skid, in order?

answer.text: In a skid you first steer toward the rear's slide and then steer back as the car straightens, so the two steering moves happen in sequence.

teaching.text: First steer toward the rear's slide, then steer back as the car straightens. Remember: toward the slide, then back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a skid you first steer toward the rear's slide and then steer back as the car straightens, so the two steering moves happen in sequence.

question.text: What should you do if a head-on crash seems likely?

answer.text: If a crash seems likely, sound the horn, keep right and turn away from oncoming traffic, even into an open field off the road.

teaching.text: If a crash seems likely, sound the horn, keep right and turn away from oncoming traffic, even into a field. Remember: horn, keep right, turn away.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a crash seems likely, sound the horn, keep right and turn away from oncoming traffic, even into an open field off the road.

question.text: What should you do if you are about to be hit from behind with clear road ahead?

answer.text: If you are about to be struck from behind with clear road ahead, accelerate away, be ready to brake if space runs out, brace yourself and press your head against the head rest.

teaching.text: About to be hit from behind with clear road ahead, accelerate away, be ready to brake, and brace with your head on the rest. Remember: speed away, then brace.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you are about to be struck from behind with clear road ahead, accelerate away, be ready to brake if space runs out, brace yourself and press your head against the head rest.

question.text: What two things should you do when a rear impact is coming?

answer.text: If a rear impact is coming and the road ahead is clear you accelerate away, but you also brace and press your head against the head rest.

teaching.text: Move forward if the road is clear, and brace with your head against the head rest. Remember: accelerate away and brace.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a rear impact is coming and the road ahead is clear you accelerate away, but you also brace and press your head against the head rest.

question.text: What should you do with the steering wheel when you are about to be hit?

answer.text: If you are about to be hit, hold the steering wheel tightly.

teaching.text: Hold the steering wheel tightly if you are about to be hit. Remember: hold the wheel tight.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you are about to be hit, hold the steering wheel tightly.

question.text: What last-resort step protects you from breaking glass?

answer.text: If a crash is about to happen, be ready to turn quickly to try to control the car, and as a last resort shield your face from breaking glass with your arms and hands.

teaching.text: Be ready to turn to control the car, and as a last resort shield your face from glass. Remember: shield your face.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a crash is about to happen, be ready to turn quickly to try to control the car, and as a last resort shield your face from breaking glass with your arms and hands.

question.text: Who is protected from civil liability for helping at a crash?

answer.text: North Carolina law shields people who stop to help at a crash from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct.

teaching.text: State law shields people who help at a crash from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct. Remember: helpers are protected.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: North Carolina law shields people who stop to help at a crash from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct.

question.text: What must a driver involved in a crash do immediately?

answer.text: A driver involved in a crash must stop immediately; failing to stop breaks the law.

teaching.text: Every driver involved in a crash must stop immediately. Remember: always stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver involved in a crash must stop immediately; failing to stop breaks the law.

question.text: What should happen at a crash scene?

answer.text: At a crash scene, take steps to prevent further crashes, help the injured and make sure someone notifies law enforcement right away.

teaching.text: At the scene, prevent further crashes, help the injured, and make sure law enforcement is notified. Remember: prevent, help, notify.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a crash scene, take steps to prevent further crashes, help the injured and make sure someone notifies law enforcement right away.

question.text: If no one is hurt, what should drivers do with cars that can be driven?

answer.text: If nobody is hurt or killed in a crash on a highway lane, ramp or shoulder, each car that can be driven safely should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder.

teaching.text: If no one is hurt, move drivable cars out of the travel lane onto the shoulder. Remember: move to the shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If nobody is hurt or killed in a crash on a highway lane, ramp or shoulder, each car that can be driven safely should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder.

question.text: When must a crash be reported to law enforcement right away?

answer.text: You must report a crash to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency right away if anyone is killed or injured or total property damage appears to be one thousand dollars or more.

teaching.text: Report right away to law enforcement for any death or injury, or apparent damage of one thousand dollars or more. Remember: injury or a thousand dollars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must report a crash to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency right away if anyone is killed or injured or total property damage appears to be one thousand dollars or more.

question.text: What can happen if you do not report a reportable crash?

answer.text: Not reporting a reportable crash can lead to prosecution and suspension of your driver license.

teaching.text: Failing to report a reportable crash can bring prosecution and license suspension. Remember: no report, lose license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Not reporting a reportable crash can lead to prosecution and suspension of your driver license.

question.text: Who else should you report a crash to, and what forms may be needed?

answer.text: You should also report any crash to your insurance company, and in some cases you must file DMV forms proving liability insurance.

teaching.text: Report any crash to your insurer, and some cases also require DMV insurance forms. Remember: tell your insurer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You should also report any crash to your insurance company, and in some cases you must file DMV forms proving liability insurance.

question.text: How does the police reporting rule differ from reporting to your insurer?

answer.text: A crash must be reported to police right away for any death or injury, or for apparent damage of one thousand dollars or more, while reporting to your insurer is advised for every crash.

teaching.text: Police reporting has the injury and damage threshold, while insurers should hear about every crash. Remember: police for serious, insurer always.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A crash must be reported to police right away for any death or injury, or for apparent damage of one thousand dollars or more, while reporting to your insurer is advised for every crash.

question.text: What information must you give and collect after a crash?

answer.text: After a crash you must give your name, address, license number, vehicle registration number and insurance company, and collect the same from the others involved.

teaching.text: Give and collect names, addresses, license numbers, registration numbers and insurance companies. Remember: swap names, licenses, insurance.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After a crash you must give your name, address, license number, vehicle registration number and insurance company, and collect the same from the others involved.

question.text: What should you do if you cannot identify the other people or the property owner?

answer.text: If you cannot identify the other occupants or the owner of damaged property, write down everything you can and give it to the nearest law enforcement officer.

teaching.text: If you cannot identify the others or the property owner, write down what you can and give it to the nearest officer. Remember: write it down for police.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you cannot identify the other occupants or the owner of damaged property, write down everything you can and give it to the nearest law enforcement officer.
